tagline.text: A travertine terrace waterfall hidden deep in the mountains of Tineg, Abra, open only in the rainy season

location.label: Location
location.text: Sitio Kaparkan, Barangay Caganayan, Tineg, Abra

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: 1–2 days (2 nights and 3 days including the overnight bus from Manila)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱4,700~6,500 (per person, including bus and tour from Manila)

children.text: Kaparkan Falls is a waterfall deep in the mountains of Tineg, the northernmost town of Abra, where blue water flows over white travertine terraces. It opens only when the water is full, from July to November, and you can reach it only on a tour approved by the local government, riding a monster truck.

Kaparkan Falls (also called Mulawin Falls) lies in Sitio Kaparkan, Barangay Caganayan, in the municipality of Tineg, the northernmost municipality of Abra in the Cordillera Administrative Region. As spring water rich in lime flows downhill and loses carbon dioxide, calcium carbonate builds up and has formed travertine terraces that stretch for hundreds of meters, each step holding a turquoise pool. Often compared to Pamukkale in Türkiye, the site sits in forest far from any village, so it feels far wilder.
The biggest catch is that you cannot go just any time. In the dry season the terraces dry out, so the local government closes the site and accepts visitors only during the rainy months of roughly
July–November
. The route is rough too. From Bangued you ride a six-wheeled monster truck up an unpaved mountain road for close to
2–3 hours

, then walk down through the forest at the end. For that reason it is hard to go on your own, and booking through a tour operator that works with the local government unit (LGU) has become the practical standard.

The reward is worth it. As you wade from one warm pool to the next, ankle-deep to waist-deep, going up and down the terraces, all you hear is the sound of thin sheets of water sliding over white rock. Roughly halfway up stands an old banyan tree whose branches and roots are coated in limestone, a favorite photo spot. Each group is given about
3 hours
at the falls, so it pays to start early and use the time well.
From Manila, many travelers take an overnight bus of about
8–10 hours

to Bangued and head straight up to the falls the same day. Because that is physically demanding, we recommend resting a night in Abra or combining the trip with Vigan in nearby Ilocos Sur for 2 nights and 3 days. Fees, rules, and whether the falls are open change from year to year, so be sure to check the latest announcement from the Abra tourism office or your tour operator before you leave.
White travertine steps stretch for about
, each step holding turquoise water. Walking up the terraces one pool at a time and swimming is the core experience here.

This huge tree stands in the middle of the terraces, its roots and branches hardened by limestone and turned white. It is said to be more than a hundred years old, and most visitors take group photos here.

The truck ride over the unpaved mountain road is an adventure in itself. It shakes a lot, so a seat next to the driver is far more comfortable, while riding on the truck bed leaves you exposed to sun and rain.
After getting off the truck, you walk down a forest trail to the falls. Reports of the walking time vary, but it is usually described as around
15–30 minutes
, and it is slippery with mud and tree roots when it rains.

blocks.title: The drop toward the Tineg River

children.text: The water flows down into the Tineg River below. The elevation difference from the spring to the river is described as about
, and the whole terrace system runs long down the mountainside.

blocks.title: Open in the rainy season only

children.text: It opens only when the water is full, which makes it rare and special. Water volume is highest in August and September, but visitor numbers are also highest then, so book early.
Rules such as the ban on single-use plastic and the mandatory guide keep damage low. At the orientation, visitors learn how to step on the travertine and to carry their trash out.

items.title: Day-trip plan
items.subtitle: From the early-morning meeting in Bangued to three hours at the falls

children.text: Take the overnight bus from the Cubao terminal in Manila to Bangued. Buses usually leave between
and arrive around
At the Bangued meeting point (depending on the tour, the DPWH office or a nearby restaurant), you register, sign a liability waiver, and attend a short orientation. Bring a government-issued ID.
Board the monster trucks and set off. The first stretch is paved and the rest is a rough mountain road. The total ride is said to take
2–3 hours
, depending on the section.
Get off the truck and walk down the forest trail to the falls. Once there, follow your guide's instructions and swim up the terrace pools in the designated areas.
When your allotted time ends, climb back to the trucks and return to Bangued. Eat lunch from a packed meal you brought, at the designated rest area.
Shower and change in Bangued, then have a late meal of Abra-style miki noodles. Take the evening overnight bus back to Manila.
A day trip is very tiring. If your schedule allows, it is much easier to stay a night in Bangued and set out early the next morning.

items.title: 2 nights and 3 days at an easy pace
items.subtitle: Abra town sights together with the falls

children.text: Take the overnight bus from Manila, and on arrival in Bangued drop off your bags at your hotel. In the afternoon, take a relaxed look around town, including Bangued Cathedral, the San Lorenzo Ruiz Shrine, and the viewpoint on Casamata Hill.
Meet early in the morning and head up to Kaparkan Falls. Swim for three hours, then return in the afternoon and rest.
Visit the Gabriela Silang Gallery in Tayum or a nearby town, then head toward Ilocos Sur to see
Vigan
before returning to Manila.
The falls trip can be cancelled depending on the weather, so it is safest to keep a spare day.
Buses from Manila (Cubao and Pasay) run to Bangued, including Partas, Dominion, and Viron. The overnight ride takes
8–10 hours
, and fares are reported at around
depending on bus class.
Buses often leave around
and arrive around
, so you can go straight to the meeting point.
If you drive yourself, take NLEX and SCTEX to Tarlac, then MacArthur Highway through Pangasinan and La Union, and turn onto the Abra–Ilocos Norte road.
Bus schedules and fares change often, so check the latest information at the terminal or on an online booking site.
Partas also runs direct buses from Baguio to Bangued. A few trips leave each day, and the ride is reported to take about
6–7 hours
If you are already traveling in the Cordillera, taking a night bus from Baguio takes less time than coming from Manila.
From the Bangued bus terminal to the meeting point is a short tricycle ride, reported at about

From the meeting point you ride a monster truck (a six-wheeled truck) up an unpaved mountain road. Whether the departure point is in Bangued town, Blugas in Tayum, or the Silaoen registration center in Lagayan depends on the operator and the season, so confirm when you book.
You can also hike up on foot, but the route passes through restricted forest, so a guide and a permit are required.
Travel time varies greatly with road conditions and weather. The truck ride is said to have taken as long as 5 hours in the past.
Abra has no airport. The nearest international airport is Laoag International Airport (LAO) in Ilocos Norte; fly from Manila to Laoag, then continue overland to Bangued.
Buses and vans run from Laoag and Vigan to Bangued.

Kaparkan Falls is beautiful only when water flows over the travertine. In the dry season the terraces dry up, so the local government blocks entry and generally takes bookings only during the rainy months of
July–November

The time with the most water and relatively clear skies is described as late August to early September. On the other hand, typhoons bring landslide and flash flood danger and trips get cancelled, so keep a spare day.

There are no hotels or restaurants near the falls, so most visitors stay in Bangued town. There are a few options, from budget hotels to garden resorts, and because the falls trip starts with an early-morning meeting, a place close to the terminal and meeting point is convenient. Book early in peak season.

For food, try Abra-style miki (a noodle dish in a thick broth) and tapsilog in Bangued. Food options at the falls are limited, so bring a packed lunch, drinking water, and snacks in advance. Because of the single-use plastic rule, you need a reusable bottle and a sturdy food container.
Registration is possible only through the Abra tourism office or an accredited tour operator (such as ABRAmazing Tours). Walk-ins are not accepted, so book several weeks ahead.
Weekday tours often have a minimum group size, and many trips run mainly on weekends. Look for weekend slots first.
You will need an ID and a signed waiver. Bring a government-issued ID, either a copy or the original.
Wear aqua shoes or sandals that can get wet. The terrace edges may have slippery moss, and thin sandals can break in the flowing water.
Small single-use water bottles are not allowed. Bring a reusable bottle of at least
1.5 liters
and a sturdy food container.
Bring a waterproof bag, sunscreen, insect repellent, and a change of clothes. There are almost no changing areas, so many people change at their Bangued hotel or the meeting point.
The seat next to the driver is the most comfortable in a monster truck. The truck bed is exposed to sun and rain and shakes a lot.
Mobile signal drops out for long stretches, so it helps to download offline maps and share your itinerary with someone.
The falls open in a rainy period, so sudden flash floods and landslides are a risk. If the sound of the water changes or the sky darkens quickly, move to higher ground at once and follow your guide.
A guide is mandatory. The travertine edges are thin and can break, so use only the designated paths and swimming areas.
Life jackets are reported not to be provided. If you are a weak swimmer, stay in the shallow pools next to your guide.
You may meet snakes and insects in the forest. Non-venomous snake bites have been reported before, so watch where you step.
The nearest hospital is in Bangued, and an injury means a long truck ride down. Bring your own first-aid supplies.
Swimming in the Tineg River has been announced as prohibited, so do not enter the water outside the designated areas.
Trips may be cancelled or changed depending on the road, the weather, and decisions of the local government. Check the latest announcement before departure.
In the provincial capital of Abra you can visit the cathedral, the San Lorenzo Ruiz Shrine, and the viewpoint on Casamata Hill in turn; they are all within town, so half a day is enough.
A historic town with the Gabriela Silang Gallery and a church, close to Bangued.
A tunnel attraction close to Abra town, good for a stop after the falls trip.
The World Heritage city in Ilocos Sur, a good place to end your trip by walking its Spanish-style streets in
Vigan
